panels.title: Tools Dropped at Registration
panels.description: MCP tools dropped while building their adapter. A drop removes a capability with nothing user-visible to say why: the assistant simply answers that it cannot do the thing. Any non-zero value is a real regression -- read `mcp_tool_registration_failed` in Loki for the server and tool names. A flat 0 line is the healthy state (the `or vector(0)` fallback: a labelled counter that never fired exposes NO series, which would render as 'No data').

panels.title: Refresh writes lost, superseded or contended
panels.description: write_lost = another writer stored its token first (its token is served). revocation_superseded = an invalid_grant for a token rotated meanwhile: no disconnection. write_contended / revocation_contended = a caller's open transaction held the row past OAUTH_REFRESH_WRITE_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS: expected 0, investigate the caller.

panels.title: Contacts results per query (p50/p95)
panels.description: Number of contacts returned per query (1h window). A p95 stuck at 0 means queries systematically miss.

panels.title: Push Notifications by Outcome
panels.description: Google push webhook outcomes. The ignored_unknown / ignored_bad_token buckets are the security signal: someone probing the public endpoint.

panels.title: Push Channel Sync (ensured / errors)
panels.description: Watch ensure/renew sweep results. A rising error series means channels are silently lapsing back to polling (expired domain verification, revoked credentials).

panels.title: Web Risk Checks by Outcome
panels.description: URL screening before web fetch / browser navigation. cache_hit costs nothing; error means fail-open (browsing unaffected, screening lost); flagged = blocked URLs.

panels.title: Email digest outcomes (by result)
panels.description: Every message handed to the e-mail digest step (detail=summary, ADR-287). 'hit' costs nothing; 'computed' is one short model call then cached; 'failed' a model refusal (the body is served instead, nothing invented); 'skipped_quota' a ceiling refusal; 'skipped_disabled' the operator switch; 'skipped_empty' a message with no body. A rising 'failed' share names a model that cannot hold the schema; a 'computed' share that never falls names a cache that never hits.

panels.title: Email attachment readings (by route and outcome)
panels.description: Every mail attachment the assistant was asked to read (get_email_attachment). 'text' costs no model call; 'vision' is one paid call to the vision slot; 'none' was refused before any reading. A rising 'failed' or 'unsupported' share names what people send that the extractors cannot read; 'skipped_quota' is a ceiling refusal, 'truncated' a vision answer cut at its budget (a refusal, never invented text).

panels.title: Files and answers sent by e-mail (by route and outcome)
panels.description: Every « Send by e-mail » from the chat or the gallery. 'mailbox' leaves through the person's connected mailbox, 'relay' through the instance's own relay to their verified address, 'none' was refused before a road was known. A rising 'refused' names a provider rejecting what it is handed, 'failed' a road that could not be reached, 'reconnect' a mailbox whose connection expired, 'too_large' files past what the road carries.

panels.title: Recipient suggestions — address-book reads (by outcome)
panels.description: The address-book reads behind the recipient suggestions of « Send by e-mail ». 'live' read a contacts provider (one consultation filed on the email_share surface, ADR-263); 'cached' opened nothing; 'no_connector' is an account without a contacts connector; 'failed' and 'timeout' left the field without suggestions.

panels.title: Catalogue Cache Decisions
panels.description: User MCP catalogue lookups by decision: hit reuses the current snapshot; miss discovers a new account/server; age, configuration and forced request rediscovery. These count lookup decisions, not successful discoveries. Schema age is separate from idle eviction. All accounts and servers are aggregated: the bounded metric has no server_name label and is independent of the MCP server selector.

panels.title: Unusable Declared Semantic Values
panels.description: Received MCP scalar values incompatible with a known declared email, calendar date, timezone datetime or URI format. invalid_type means the received scalar has the wrong type; invalid_format means its text cannot be used under that format. Counts are values, not failed calls. Canonical results remain intact and unusable paths are published beside them. All servers/accounts are aggregated; this bounded metric does not follow the MCP server selector. A flat zero is the healthy state, including when no invalid value has exposed a labelled series.

panels.title: Catalogue snapshot publications, by outcome
panels.description: Conditional writes of a personal MCP server's catalogue snapshot: published, or refused because the row was edited (configuration_changed), switched off (inactive), deleted (missing), or already holds a newer discovery (superseded). Per hour.

panels.title: Personal read_me fetches at real use, by outcome
panels.description: A personal server's read_me fetched when the pipeline planner prepares a turn about it (spec 2026-10-21 §5.5b): fetched, empty (no text), failed, timed_out (bounded by MCP_USER_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) or busy (another worker held the claim). Discovery never calls read_me.

panels.title: Personal server preparation p95 (s), by source and outcome
panels.description: One personal MCP server prepared for a turn (spec 2026-10-21 §5.3): source catalogue = this worker's entry or the persisted snapshot (no network), network = a discovery bounded by MCP_USER_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS. A server still discovering at MCP_USER_PREPARATION_CEILING_SECONDS is left out of the turn and observed when it finishes.

panels.title: Background catalogue revalidations, by outcome
panels.description: An aged personal catalogue is served and revalidated in the background (spec 2026-10-21 §5.4): published, refused by the row (configuration_changed, inactive, missing, superseded), skipped (busy = another worker holds the claim, claim_unavailable = no cache, paused) or failed / timed_out (which feeds the failure pause).

panels.title: Tool declarations checked at use, by outcome
panels.description: A call built from a personal catalogue past its server's ttlMs is checked in its own session first (spec 2026-10-21 §5.5): identical (the entry becomes verified), compatible (sent, revalidation scheduled), or refused unsent — missing, incompatible (arguments no longer valid), tightened (newly destructive). A refusal reaches the model as CONFLICT.
